headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.8245). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 17 studies yielded an effect size of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.83–1.04), indicating no statistically significant association between Vitamin C and breast cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 83.62%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
